key_insight: Increasing Y content in BCFZY cathodes modestly improves proton transport under PCFC operating gases, while low oxygen partial pressure is predicted to shift transport from hydroxyl to hydride species.
engineering_relevance: Cathode optimization should account for gas conditions because Y doping alone offers only modest predicted proton-conductivity gains under PCFC operating conditions.
method: Used ab initio molecular dynamics to assess proton tracer diffusivity across three compositions with Y fractions of 0, 0.1, and 0.2.
Modeled temperature-dependent proton concentrations using hydration, oxidation, and hydride-formation defect equilibria.
Separated diffusivity and concentration contributions to proton conductivity.
evidence_signal: At 500 °C, increasing Y from BCFZ to BCFY yielded predicted gains of 1.7% in proton diffusivity, 3.8% in proton concentration, and 5.3% in proton conductivity under PCFC operating gas conditions.
watch_item: These computational predictions require experimental validation under matched gas conditions; larger gains reported in reducing atmospheres may not transfer to PCFC cathode operation.
paper_title: Effects of Yttrium doping on Proton Conductivity in Ba(Fe, Co, Zr, Y)O$_{3-δ}$ Cathode Materials for Proton Ceramic Fuel Cells
